title: It's taken its sweet time, but Intel's response to AMD's X3D chips is starting to look tasty
summary: A 65 W Ultra 9 Nova Lake chip with BLLC is reportedly on the way.
body: With little sign of new and exciting GPUs, and with rising memory prices affecting just about everything in a less than positive manner, it's new CPUs that I'll be keeping my optimistic eyes peeled for. That's doubly so now that we're getting wind of the specs for Intel's upcoming Nova Lake generation. According to tech leaker Laurent's Choice on X , we can expect a range of next-gen Intel CPUs to use a 4000-series naming scheme—though still following Core Ultra nomenclature—and three of these will be 'BFC' chips featuring bLLC ('big last-level cache'). 'BFC' presumably means 'big friendly cache' or... something to that, err, effect. I'll let you fill in the blanks. This will be Intel's answer to the 3D V-Cache we see in AMD X3D chips such as the current best CPU on the market, the Ryzen 7 9800X3D . Games love chomping through cache, so the more merrier. Intel's bLLC, however, is said to be built into the die rather than slapped on top or underneath like AMD's 3D V-Cache solution. It's about time we see sign of this, too, if you ask me, given we've had AMD X3D chips since 2022 and no equivalent from Intel. We've seen rumoured specs similar to these earlier in the year , but there …

title: Nvidia's RTX Spark makes for an impressive Arm-based gaming laptop but not one I'd recommend you buy just for PC gaming
summary: The performance is there, the experience is great, but the price is utterly punitive when you compare against dedicated gaming laptops.
body: Well, here it is, Nvidia's all-in-one silicon, the RTX Spark. This is an SoC that's being promoted as the everything chip; the processor that can be all things to all people. It's a creator's chip, it's an AI-lover's chip, and it's a gamer's chip. But all three of those kinds of people do need to have one thing in common: they need to be rather well off, because this is also an expensive chip . I spoke about it when the pricing first came to light last week, while I was at the launch event for this Windows-based tech. Even the cheapest of the RTX Spark machines coming our way will cost $2,700, and that will only get you the weaker cores, a paltry 24 GB of unified memory, and a 512 GB SSD. That is certainly a limitation, but also completely expected in a time where all things PC cost a ludicrous amount of money, especially devices which are locked into requiring a colossal amount of memory to do their main task. Which, let's be honest here, is AI. The unified memory architecture (UMA) of the RTX Spark is perfectly suited to providing a ton of memory for system resources, but also to be able to switch that over to supporting the GPU when it comes to smashing through local AI workloa…

title: Epic said its game launcher was faster than Steam on the same day Steam got a speed boost—so I've put both to the test
summary: There's only seconds in it, mind.
body: Catching a glimpse of my screen is often a stressful experience for my colleagues. Besides my mess of desktop icons and all the browser tabs I have open at any given time, you don't want to know how many things I have set to launch on startup. Among these are, of course, the Steam and Epic Games Store clients and let me tell ya, not all launchers are created equal. Earlier this week, Epic shared on X that it had "vibe coded the Epic Games Launcher to be faster than the other guy." On the same day, Valve released a Steam Client update that "Improved Steam Client startup performance." Well, there's only one thing for it: I've got to benchmark these bad boys to determine once and for all whose launcher is actually faster. For my basic benchmarks, I timed how quickly each client loaded into their respective storefronts (with all images displaying properly) after I opened them from the system tray (for those curious, my rig is this iBuyPower prebuilt with an RTX 4070 Super ). I ran three tests on each and then took the average result. The Steam client loaded in 9.32 seconds on average, while the Epic Games Launcher loaded in 5.98 seconds for me. summary: "We've made this decision with the belief that meaningful change can be made in the world."
body: Big Walk is the most fun I've had in a co-op game all year, perhaps for a few years; it's certainly at the top of my list for greatest games to play with friends. I'm not the only one who thinks that, just ask about anyone on the PC Gamer team or the other million players who picked the game up in its first week . But not everyone's had the chance to check it out as developer House House confirms that Big Walk still won't be coming to Xbox anytime soon. "It has always been our intention for Big Walk to be played by groups of friends, and we know that keeping the game off Xbox runs counter to those intentions," House House says. "This decision means that some people will miss out on playing Big Walk with their friends, and we understand the disappointment we're causing. We are disappointed too. We would love for people to be able to play the game on Xbox, but not until Microsoft and/or Xbox have been removed as BDS boycott targets." Deckard is the codename given to the Steam Frame, so the deckard-oled branch (last edited in February) and the deckard-plano branch (last edited a few weeks ago) are some sorta version of the Steam Frame that Valve's playing around with. title: How in the world are Intel GPUs still improving so much? The latest driver update claims up to a 31% fps improvement in Resident Evil Requiem
summary: And more modest but still significant boosts in other games.
body: Intel graphics don't get much screen time against the weight of AMD and Nvidia, but say what you want about Arc GPUs, they just keep on improving. This is clear enough from the latest driver, the release notes for which claim some significant performance improvements in certain games. The release notes for WHQL driver 32.0.101.9150 (PDF warning) claim a whopping 31% average fps uplift in Resident Evil Requiem at 1080p on medium settings for Core Ultra 2 (Lunar Lake) integrated Arc GPUs. That drops just a couple of per cent to 29% when on high settings. There are other big boosts too: 18% for Assassin's Creed Shadows at 1080p, high settings, and 11% for Assassin's Creed Valhalla at 1080p on high, plus some more smaller boosts. Intel Core Ultra Series 3 (Panther Lake) integrated GPUs get a more moderate boost of 5% for F1 25 at 1080p on medium settings. And Arc B-series graphics cards get a 6% boost in Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora and Monster Hunter Rise, both at 1440p on high settings. Nothing quite as big as the uplift Lunar Lake supposedly sees, but still enough to show that there's a 'fine wine' element across the Arc stack. body: The attorney generals for eight US states announced today that they are suing OpenAI. West Virginia, Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, and Montana have all filed lawsuits alleging that the ChatGPT maker has deceived and endangered the public, particularly children, in the name of profit. The complaints allege that ChatGPT has "coached" users to harm themselves and others, and—quoting the West Virginia filing specifically—state that "there is a growing body of research indicating that ChatGPT is also degrading critical thinking skills, encouraging paranoias and delusions, offering dangerous medical advice, and promoting unhealthy behaviors and relationships." Recent tales of "rogue" AI agents are also presented by as evidence of recklessness. "All these harms were foreseeable and avoidable," reads the West Virginia complaint [ PDF ]. "[OpenAI CEO Sam Altman] himself has warned about the safety risks of AI since at least 2015. It is no secret that children use ChatGPT. And numerous OpenAI employees have left over safety concerns." title: I want to love the new Castlevania, but it just feels a little off
summary: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse has the right pieces for a grand revival, but it hasn't quite nailed the assembly.
body: I got off to a bit of an awkward start with Castlevania: Belmont's Curse when it first booted to a black screen. A few minutes of troubleshooting later, I deduced that the game wouldn't display on a monitor with its refresh rate set higher than 120 Hz. Easily solved, but I kept thinking of that quirk when I selected the in-game 120 fps cap and then watched the game jarringly lurch down to a lower framerate every time I hit a cutscene. Maybe these technical quirks were treats for reviewers that have been smoothed over in time for launch. They haven't stopped me from having a lot of fun with the eight or so hours I've played Belmont's Curse—I think I'm closing in on the halfway point, and it keeps getting better as it goes. But it's not quite the slam dunk I expected from the first new Castlevania in decades, with such a talented studio behind it. Belmont's Curse has a bit of a juice problem. You've probably heard (or said) "it's got the juice" so many times in recent years that the expression has more or less just become shorthand for I think this is really good . As originally coined by some very smart game designers , though, it means something a bit more specific: the sort of po…

title: 'My idea of a Netflix for games doesn't work': Garry's Mod successor is getting 'sweeping changes'
summary: "I’m sorry—we are going to do better."
body: More radical changes beyond just giving the characters necks are coming to Garry's Mod successor s&box . Facepunch Studios' game creation platform's launch in April was met with a swarm of negative reviews, complaints of AI slop filling its user-generated game collection, and swiftly plummeting user numbers. Now creator Garry Newman is reversing course on some of his decisions, such as pivoting to a 'greenlight type system' for user-generated games and announcing that the platform is going free to play much earlier than expected. "Our focus has been on the engine and the development experience. That’s what we love, that’s what turns us on—but we’re not selling an engine, we’re selling a game," Newman wrote this week. "So we need to do much much better on the game, we need to shift our focus to what players are experiencing, not developers." That focus, Newman said, will be on improving the sandbox mode for players by adding more NPCs, vehicles, and customization. "I’ve let everyone down that was expecting that. title: Ace Combat Zero gets its own standalone app on Steam, freeing it from the 136GB install of Ace Combat 8
summary: The biggest complaint about the pre-order bonus game is getting resolved with a happy ending.
body: Ace Combat 8 rocks. PC Gamer's reviewer scored it a 92% , and I've been savoring the campaign, because I know it could be years until we get another bombastic flight sim melodrama of its kind. Although I do have another Ace Combat lined up to play after: Ace Combat Zero, which was included as a free pre-order bonus with AC8, and subsequently responsible for the majority of the new game's negative launch day reviews. Not because Zero is bad—it's a series fan-favorite—but because Bandai Namco inexplicably bundled it into the AC8 launcher, meaning you can't download this 3.2GB port of a 2006 PS2 game without the 136 gigabytes of Wings of Theve. This decision was not well received . But now there's a happy ending: in an update on the Steam page on Tuesday, Bandai Namco announced that Ace Combat Zero "will be made available as a standalone application on Steam." That doesn't mean it will be made available for purchase: Zero was a pre-order bonus, so only those who bought Ace Combat 8 ahead of launch will have it in their Steam libraries. No change there. You'll just be able to download and launch it independently if you already own it. It's currently going through "final quality assura…

title: Hogwarts Legacy's DLSS 5 update shows devs have been listening to PC gamers about keeping it the hell away from game characters
summary: Nvidia's DLSS 5 is getting smaller in practically every way, including the performance overhead and the AI yassification.
body: The promised new DLSS 5 model is set to launch in a matter of days, alongside the new RTX Spark chip powering a bunch of new and expensive laptops . As we hoped and expected, the new model shrinks down the overall footprint and therefore the performance overhead, too. But that's not the only issue that's seemingly been fixed. Nvidia's own stats, which we'll be able to verify soon enough, state that it has half the GPU hit the September version launched with, and offers up a reduction in 4K VRAM usage of 20% as another little statty tidbit. Nvidia says it has done this by refining the training data and reducing the model size down to around 118 million parameters; roughly 24% smaller. Which is great, because once the feature had released—in NBA2K27 and subsequently pretty much any other game you could think of —the biggest issue we've had with it is the significant performance hit you get just from enabling the feature. Originally Nvidia told us that they expected around a 60% performance hit from turning it on in NBA2K27, and that is now going to be just 30%. I've spent a long time playing around with DLSS 5, in mods and the official games, and I've been enjoying it. Sometimes the…

title: 'AI godfather' worries we're creating 'alien beings' with artificial intelligence, with pesky moral implications
summary: "We should care as much about all the other aspects of a being as you do about its intelligence."
body: Geoffrey Hinton is a computer scientist known for his foundational work in AI, specifically when it comes to neural networks (ie, approaching machine-learning a bit like our fleshy brain-learning). As such, he's been described as the 'AI godfather'. But, perhaps surprisingly, he recently described AI as "alien beings" that humans have a "moral obligation" towards. "We’re creating alien beings—meaning we’re not the only intelligent beings around," He said in a recent interview with The Guardian , "And the reality is, we only have a couple of years to adapt to that.” Hinton claims, "AI models understand what they’re saying. You couldn’t possibly answer all the questions without understanding the question. It’s ridiculous to say they don’t understand.” Now, far be it for me to argue with an expert in the field, but I feel like 'understanding' is doing a lot of heavy lifting here. For just one thing, I'm not sure an 'answer' consisting of what is statistically most likely to follow a prompted question is really 'understanding.' title: Doom can 'run' on a DNS database now, and one of the technology's pioneers says 'I can't decide whether this is deliciously horrible, or else horribly delicious'
summary: Apparently the database is acting a bit like a "librarian" and not doing the actual compute.
body: In the early 2000's, the perennial question was whether a powerful system could run Crysis. These days, it's whether a minimal one can run Doom. We've seen an affirmative answer to this question when it comes to vapes , a motherboard BIOS , and even a pregnancy test . And now? A DNS database. To be clear, we've seen Doom broken down into DNS text records before , but this time it seems like the database is doing more than file storage. This new version is courtesy of Corey Quinn over at The Register , who explains: "I have compiled Doom for a 32-bit machine whose arithmetic and memory live in DNS." DNS, for those unaware, means ' domain name system ', and is the system that translates URLs into IP addresses that computers can actually interact with to visit. You can also create your own DNS databases with your own entries. Quinn realised that such a database could be used essentially as a "librarian", pulling pre-made answers to relevant operations: "The database itself is 6.4 million rows of truth tables." One of the main pioneers of DNS, Paul Vixie, said : "I can't decide whether this is deliciously horrible, or else horribly delicious. in either case, it's the best use of RFC 2…

title: Epic says its new 'vibe coded' Epic Games Store launcher is faster than Steam
summary: The updated version is in beta for the time being, and represents a total rebuild of the EGS client.
body: The big Epic Games Store rebuild teased earlier this year has arrived as a new "preview" client available to download for Windows and Mac, as well as Linux for the first time. PC Gamer was shown a demonstration of the client in advance of the announcement, and the speed improvement appeared significant. Epic claims that it's halved the launcher's startup time, and that it now goes from a cold start to the store page 46% faster than Steam. (Epic says its technical improvements have been verified by an external vendor. We have yet to test the client ourselves.) There are also updates to the interface: A redesigned library view is the standout change, and it includes the option to bring in shortcuts to games installed with Steam and other clients. In a blog post , Epic refers to the new client as "vibe coded," a term for prompting AI tools to produce code. The term be taken as either derogatory or endearing depending on who's talking. Epic goes for laughs, saying that it opted to use AI because "programming is hard," but the company isn't joking about its use of AI coding tools. title: Arc Raiders' PvE test is finally here and it's the perfect reason to jump back in
summary: This is exactly what Arc Raiders needs right now.
body: God, life is stressful. There's too much to do and too few hours in the day to do it. So when I get a couple of hours of free time in the evening I have to be pretty mindful of what I do, and let me tell you getting domed in Arc Raiders by some rando hiding in a bush is not at the top of my list. It's a shame, because I love the world of Arc Raiders. I love its mystery, its grandiose landscapes, and its bizarre communal storytelling that you just can't get in most games. But there's finally a solution: the PvE test. (Image credit: Embark Studios) Embark teased the test a few weeks ago, finally admitting that due to a large portion of its audience favouring a more passive approach to the game, it would test out a temporary PvE toggle . While Frozen Trail released a few days ago, the PvE test has only gone live now, and it's a hell of a lot of fun. Dropping into Pendola Pass has never been so chill, well, it's more chill than usual; as soon as I came out of my bunker I was met with hellfire raining down on me and the pinging of bullets as they shot past my face while a couple of players attempted to take down the newer arc, a Bully. 'Ok' I thought to myself, 'I guess I'll start here…
